name: Jutland Current
scope: Danish west-coast reference corridor from an OSW German Bight approach gate to an offshore northern-Jutland/Skagerrak approach gate. Excludes upstream English Channel and southern North Sea circuits, Baltic Current inflow and Norwegian Coastal Current continuation. No North/South Jutland branch lengths or aliases admitted.
layer: Regional near-surface coastal naming context; not Atlantic bottom-water inflows or a reconstructed depth-specific core.
time_convention: General regional circulation descriptions in 2015 and 2024 research papers. Not a contemporaneous trajectory, annual mean axis or seasonal route series; source sea-level seasonality is not a current-length measurement.
source_locator: Section 1.3: Jutland Current transports material north along Danish coast into Skagerrak; subsequent Baltic/Norwegian coastal circulation is distinct. Figure 1 caption labels North and South Jutland currents separately; neither is silently merged as an alias here.
source_citation: Lenz et al. (2024), Provenance of clay-sized detrital sediments in the North Sea and the Skagerrak region based on radiogenic Nd-Sr-Hf isotopes and clay mineral compositions: assessing the impact of coastal and seabed erosion, Frontiers in Marine Science 11, doi:10.3389/fmars.2024.1416519.

supporting_sources.citation: Passaro et al. (2015), Annual sea level variability of the coastal ocean: The Baltic Sea-North Sea transition zone, doi:10.1002/2014JC010510.
supporting_sources.locator: Section 2, Area of Study, first paragraph: surface Jutland flow carries Atlantic/German Bight water and turns into the Norwegian Coastal Current after encountering Baltic water.
supporting_sources.role: Surface-flow and naming-transition context; sea-level annual cycle does not supply current geometry or width.

coordinate_selection: OSW selects every offshore vertex and the bookkeeping gates at 54.8 N and northern Jutland. The source names regions and circulation but does not publish these vertices, an exact origin/termination or a full-current length. An alternative southern approach and Skagerrak gate tests endpoint convention. No source figure arrows, sediment trajectories or velocity fields digitized; offsets are editorial sensitivity only.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW southern German Bight approach and eastern offshore Skagerrak gate; neither boundary is an observed current endpoint.

scenario_rule: Two selected regional gate conventions crossed with longitude and independent endpoint latitude offsets -0.05/0/+0.05 degrees: 54 editorial scenarios, not measured endpoint or width uncertainty.
method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 54 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
